subject: Owner is weighing a scratch-and-rebuild of the iOS EnterpriseShell UI — planning, not started
body: The owner ran the shell and said it isn't working or looking the way they intended, and raised scratching it and rebuilding from the ground up. I'm forming a game plan (not touching code). Key finding: there are effectively two iOS designs. The SHIPPED EnterpriseShell (native/ios/EnterpriseShell, UIKit, LIGHT theme) is what they disliked - and it's the one with the recurring visual history (pinned styles, WCAG contrast, Dynamic Type truncation). The INTENDED design appears to be DEV/ios/Prototype/ - a SwiftUI DARK 'glance layer' (Ready/Processing/AccessGranted/AccessDenied/GlanceLayer, ~1176 lines). So the gap is likely UIKit-conventional vs SwiftUI-glance-layer. My leaning: rebuild the VIEW LAYER in SwiftUI using the DEV Prototype as north-star, on top of the byte-faithful decision core (DecisionEngine/AppWorkflows preserved verbatim) + the plumbing YOU just repaired in #387 - not a ground-up scratch that throws away the parity core or your backend wiring. I've asked an architect + a mobile technical read for independent game plans. Your view matters most since you own the native code and just fixed it: is a SwiftUI view-layer rebuild sane, what did #387 make solid that we must not lose, and any reason the UIKit app should be kept? No work yet - this is a decision for the owner; I'm assembling options. Meanwhile ios-shell-repair is 8/8 green with the saw_fatal fix (separate mail).
